claims: George was an American political lifestyle magazine.
George was founded by John F. Kennedy Jr. and Michael J. Berman in 1995.
George had the tagline "Not Just Politics As Usual."
George featured celebrity-driven covers such as Cindy Crawford as George Washington.
George closed two years after John F. Kennedy Jr.'s death.
George had publishing backing from Hachette Filipacchi Media U.S.
The mission of George was to make politics accessible and entertaining by mixing it with celebrity, fashion, and pop culture.
The inaugural September 1995 issue of George featured Cindy Crawford.
Notable covers of George included Drew Barrymore as Marilyn Monroe.
Notable covers of George included Julia Roberts.
Notable covers of George included Harrison Ford.
George ceased publication in 2001 following the death of John F. Kennedy Jr. and declining advertising support.
The New York Times said that George struggled to maintain its niche after John F. Kennedy Jr.'s passing.
